 ATP Paris Day 1 Predictions Including Denis Shapovalov vs Karen Khachanov 
 Share Share this article
 × X Facebook LinkedIn WhatsApp Reddit Email Copy 
 The first round is upon us at the ATP Paris Rolex Paris Masters , and this set of matches is headlined by a blockbuster between Denis Shapovalov and Karen Khachanov. With fresh rivalries, rematches, and ranking points all on the line, as ever, we here at LWOT will be offering our predictions for every match, but who will advance?
 ATP Paris Day 1 Predictions
 Kyrian Jacquet vs Tomas Machac
 Head-to-Head: First meeting
 Kyrian Jacquet will have the home crowd behind him, but Machac represents a considerable step up in opposition. The Czech’s ability to absorb pace, redirect the ball and move opponents around the court makes him a difficult player to attack. He also possesses the variety to adjust when an opponent tries to take control of the rallies.
 Jacquet will need to make the most of his aggressive instincts and use the occasion to play freely. However, Machac’s greater experience and tactical flexibility should allow him to manage the contest, particularly if he avoids giving the Frenchman too many opportunities to dictate.
 Prediction: Machac in 2
 Ignacio Buse vs Zizou Bergs
 Head-to-Head: Bergs 1–0 Buse
 Bergs won their only previous meeting in Shanghai last month, delivering a commanding 6–0 6–3 victory. That result will give the Belgian confidence, although Buse will be keen to show that he can offer a stronger challenge this time. The Peruvian has made encouraging progress, but he will need to improve his serving and avoid allowing Bergs to dictate from the first ball.
 Bergs’ aggressive approach and ability to take time away from opponents make him particularly dangerous on indoor hard courts. Unless Buse can find a way to disrupt his rhythm, the Belgian should have enough to advance.
 Prediction: Bergs in 2
 Luciano Darderi vs Rinky Hijikata
 Head-to-Head: Hijikata 2–1 Darderi
 Hijikata has won their two most recent meetings, beating Darderi in straight sets at Indian Wells and Cincinnati this season. The Australian’s ability to take the ball early and redirect pace has caused the Italian problems, particularly on hard courts. Darderi will need to be more proactive if he is to prevent another defeat.
 The Italian’s groundstrokes can be effective when he has time to set up and dictate, but Hijikata’s movement and willingness to step inside the baseline could deny him that comfort. Their recent meetings suggest the Australian has found a formula that works, and he should be able to carry that advantage into Paris.
 Prediction: Hijikata in 3
 Denis Shapovalov vs Karen Khachanov
 Head-to-Head: Shapovalov 2-0 Khachanov
 Mar 22, 2025; Miami, FL, USA; Denis Shapovalov (CAN) hits a backhand against Thiago Agustin Tirante (ARG)(not pictured) on day five of the Miami Open at Hard Rock Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images 
 Denis Shapovalov ’s left-handed game and ability to produce winners from difficult positions make him dangerous, but his aggressive approach can also lead to inconsistent spells. Khachanov, meanwhile, brings a more measured style, built around a heavy serve and powerful groundstrokes.
 The indoor conditions should reward both players’ first-strike tennis, making the return games particularly important. Khachanov’s ability to maintain a high level from the back of the court could give him an advantage in the longer exchanges, while Shapovalov will look to create openings with his variety and change of direction. The Russian’s greater consistency gives him a narrow edge in what could be a close encounter.
 Prediction: Khachanov in 3
